lines: \paragraph{Method-level interventions.} ICG ($\Delta \approx 0$, $p = .206$), Contrastive ($\Delta = -9.31$\,pp, $p < 0.01$), and Debate ($\Delta = -18.63$/$-23.00$\,pp, $p < 0.001$) all fail (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}, Appendix~\ref{app:remediation}). Ten further experiments (code verification, iterative refinement, logprob filtering, cross-model ensembles) produce neutral-to-negative results (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:additional_interventions}).

-\paragraph{Independence-accuracy trade-off.} Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization} compares Fleiss' $\kappa$ across four aggregation methods and three model families (Figure~\ref{fig:kappa-accuracy}). SC ($\kappa = 0.44$), Diverse-Prompt ($\kappa = 0.40$), and ICG ($\kappa = 0.47$) cluster at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$; Debate reaches $\kappa = 0.15$ but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp. All three families cluster above $\kappa = 0.40$, forming a same-model trade-off ceiling at the 7B--32B scale tested: methods that increase independence destroy accuracy, and methods preserving accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. Mistral shows the highest bias ratio ($4.97\times$), while Qwen ($3.93\times$) and LLaMA ($3.87\times$) are comparable (overlapping CIs); all three exceed $1.0$, confirming that confirmation bias is universal across families. For practitioners, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration, SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias, SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Whether 70B+ models or trained extractors shift the observed trade-off boundary remains open.

+\paragraph{Independence-accuracy trade-off.} Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization} compares Fleiss' $\kappa$ across four aggregation methods and three model families (Figure~\ref{fig:kappa-accuracy}). SC ($\kappa = 0.44$), Diverse-Prompt ($\kappa = 0.40$), and ICG ($\kappa = 0.47$) cluster at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$; Debate reaches $\kappa = 0.15$ but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp. All three families cluster above $\kappa = 0.40$, forming a same-model trade-off ceiling at the 7B--32B scale tested: methods that increase independence destroy accuracy, and methods preserving accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. The bias ratio gradient ($4.97\times$ Mistral $> 3.93\times$ Qwen $> 2.88\times$ LLaMA) suggests weaker models suffer more severe confirmation bias; all three exceed $1.0$, confirming universality across families. For practitioners, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration, SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias, SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Whether 70B+ models or trained extractors shift the observed trade-off boundary remains open.

lines: -The Symbolic Mirage operates through two channels: correlated constraints compress $K_{\text{eff}} < 2$ (\emph{direct}), while answer-coupled constraints collapse MAX-SAT to vote counting (\emph{indirect}; Eq.~\ref{eq:degenerate}). \citet{huang2024selfcorrect} and \citet{stechly2025selfverification} observe that LLMs cannot self-correct without external feedback; our bias ratio ($4.97\times$ Mistral, $3.93\times$ Qwen, $3.87\times$ LLaMA; all CIs exclude 1.0) quantifies why: extraction and generation share the same distributional biases. $\text{BR} > 1$ across three families predicts that any self-verification pipeline deriving criteria from the same model faces this bottleneck, whether formal constraints, natural-language critiques, or code assertions.

+The Symbolic Mirage operates through two channels: correlated constraints compress $K_{\text{eff}} < 2$ (\emph{direct}), while answer-coupled constraints collapse MAX-SAT to vote counting (\emph{indirect}; Eq.~\ref{eq:degenerate}). \citet{huang2024selfcorrect} and \citet{stechly2025selfverification} observe that LLMs cannot self-correct without external feedback; our bias ratio ($4.97\times$ Mistral, $3.93\times$ Qwen, $2.88\times$ LLaMA) quantifies why: extraction and generation share the same distributional biases. $\text{BR} > 1$ across three families predicts that any self-verification pipeline deriving criteria from the same model faces this bottleneck, whether formal constraints, natural-language critiques, or code assertions.

$K_{\text{eff}} = 1.20$--$3.62$ for nominal $K = 12$ means sampling beyond a dozen traces yields diminishing independent information, and the pattern intensifies with capability: Qwen3 thinking mode ($\kappa = 0.91$, $K_{\text{eff}} = 1.09$) produces near-deterministic traces, creating a scaling paradox for o1/R1-style reasoning models \citep{guo2025deepseekr1}. The $\kappa$ floor is universal---all non-destructive interventions cluster at $\kappa \geq 0.40$ (Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}), confirming a structural ceiling. This instantiates the classic ensemble tension \citep{krogh1994neural, brown2005diversity}: Debate raises $K_{\text{eff}}$ from ${\sim}1.8$ to ${\sim}4.5$ but collapses accuracy ($-18.6$\,pp, $p < 0.001$), because diversity-inducing perturbations degrade predictions rather than introducing independent reasoning. Cross-architecture escape succeeds (Spearman $\rho = 1.0$, $p = 0.003$, $n{=}6$) precisely because encoder-only DeBERTa and decoder-only LLMs have structurally different error profiles. If traces do not faithfully reflect reasoning \citep{turpin2024language}, the mirage is inherent to extraction from opaque models.

lines: This correlation manifests through a specific mechanism: self-extracted constraints systematically confirm the model's majority answer regardless of correctness. On Mistral-7B FOLIO ($n = 204$), when SICA errs, 83.3\% of extracted constraints support the incorrect majority answer---a bias ratio of $4.97\times$ compared to correct problems. Consequently, 94\% of SICA errors overlap with SC errors: symbolic aggregation adds no independent corrective signal.

-The causal chain is: the model generates an answer, then extracts logical constraints consistent with it. Constraints from majority-answer traces use trace-specific variable names (56.4\% of cross-answer pairs share zero Z3 variables), so MAX-SAT retains nearly all, and aggregation reduces to a weighted majority vote (Eq.~\ref{eq:degenerate}). Confirmation bias generalizes across model families: bias ratios of $4.97\times$ (Mistral-7B), $3.93\times$ (Qwen2.5-14B), and $3.87{\times}^{\dag}$ (LLaMA-3.1-8B) all significantly exceed $1.0$ ($^{\dag}$based on 4/12 traces due to extraction failures; Table~\ref{tab:cross-model-bias}). The oracle ceiling (\S\ref{sec:oracle}) confirms that 75.9\% of the potential gain is lost to self-extraction quality.

"We introduce the \textit{Cumulative Information Lift} (CIL) to unify our diagnostic findings under a single information-theoretic quantity:
\[
\text{CIL}(V, G) = \log \frac{P(V \text{ correct} \mid G \text{ wrong})}{P(V \text{ correct} \mid G \text{ correct})}
\]
CIL measures whether verifier $V$ provides complementary information beyond generator $G$: $\text{CIL} > 0$ indicates $V$ preferentially corrects $G$'s errors (rescue), $\text{CIL} = 0$ indicates independence (no rescue), and $\text{CIL} < 0$ indicates shared bias ($V$ fails when $G$ fails)."

**统一段**：
"CIL subsumes our key findings: (1) \textit{Symbolic Confirmation Bias} corresponds to $\text{CIL}(\text{self}, G) \approx 0$, since self-extracted constraints inherit the generator's bias; (2) the \textit{Capability Gap Corollary} predicts that $\text{CIL}(V, G) > 0$ when $V$ is architecturally independent and sufficiently capable; (3) \textit{DRC} adaptively routes to the verifier on questions where the expected CIL is highest (low SC agreement signals high $G$-uncertainty, maximizing $P(V \text{ correct} \mid G \text{ wrong})$). Across [N] generator--verifier pairs, CIL correlates [strongly/perfectly] with observed combo gain (Spearman $\rho = $ [TBD], $p < $ [TBD]), confirming that information-theoretic complementarity, not verifier accuracy alone, determines verification effectiveness."

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

We identify the Symbolic Mirage: self-extracted constraints inherit the generating model's biases ($\text{BR} = 4.97\times$, 83.3\%), explaining why twenty-seven remediation strategies fail. Oracle controls ($+29.90$/$+14.22$\,pp) confirm the mechanism is sound; the bottleneck is extraction quality, not the formal channel. Three diagnostics predict failure ($C_0 < 5\%$, SC $\leq 40\%$, process similarity). Cross-architecture NLI escapes the mirage when the verifier exceeds the generator ($\rho = 1.0$, $p = 0.003$); DRC recovers 90\% of this gain at 39\% cost.

CIL subsumes our key findings: (1)~Symbolic Confirmation Bias corresponds to $\text{CIL}(\text{self}, G) \approx 0$, since self-extracted constraints inherit the generator's bias; (2)~Observation~2 predicts $\text{CIL}(V, G) > 0$ when $V$ is architecturally independent and sufficiently capable; (3)~DRC adaptively routes to the verifier on questions where expected CIL is highest (low SC agreement signals high $G$-uncertainty, maximizing $P(V \text{ correct} \mid G \text{ wrong})$). Across [N] generator--verifier pairs, CIL correlates with observed combo gain (Spearman $\rho = $ [TBD], $p < $ [TBD]), confirming that information-theoretic complementarity, not verifier accuracy alone, determines verification effectiveness.

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   This session handles the `symb_invariant_consensus` EMNLP 2026 paper as Paper Agent. Multiple sequential Director instructions were received and executed:

   - **R10 Batch 2 (C4, C5)**: Four-layer novelty argument + three-paradigm classification in introduction.tex and related_work.tex
   - **R10 Batch 3 (W1-W4, W6-W8)**: DRC caveat, cross-arch 3 conditions, power limitation, TOST margin, SCB distinction, ToT citation, 27 strategies categorization
   - **R10 Batch 4**: Figure 2→figure*, Table 1 footnote simplification
   - **W5 BR CI + LLaMA BR**: Added bootstrap CIs, then corrected LLaMA BR 2.88→3.87, then REVERTED back to 2.88 (bootstrap used wrong definition)
   - **TOST correction**: 5/5/6 → 4/2/10 classification + sensitivity table
   - **3 new citations**: wan2025unveiling, jhaveri2026failing, miya2025eidoku with correct arXiv IDs
   - **CIL framework**: New theoretical unification paragraph in §3 method.tex with [TBD] placeholders

   **HARD CONSTRAINTS**: EMNLP 8-page main text; w=3 primary; all significance after BH correction; DeBERTa standalone=55.00%; SC baseline FOLIO=55.88%; κ=0.46; DRC unchanged.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - EMNLP 2026 ARR: 8-page main text limit, Limitations/References/Appendix exempt
   - Symbolic Confirmation Bias (SCB): BR=4.97× Mistral, 3.93× Qwen, 2.88× LLaMA
   - CIL (Cumulative Information Lift): log(P(V correct|G wrong)/P(V correct|G correct))
   - Three paradigms: specification-generation, program-generation, trace-extraction
   - TOST equivalence: 4 equivalent, 2 genuinely different (both negative), 10 underpowered
   - Cross-arch escape 3 conditions: structural independence, positive capability gap, task-verifier alignment
   - Spearman: 6-point ρ=1.0, exact permutation p=0.003 (two-tailed)
   - BH correction: m=12, only Mistral w=3 (adj p=6.78e-05) and w=5 (adj p=7.41e-06) survive
   - BR CIs: Mistral [3.98, 6.37], Qwen [2.44, 7.11], LLaMA raw CI removed (wrong definition), LLaMA weighted CI [2.19, 3.28]
   - DRC: τ=0.7 recovers 90% of gain at 39% cost (τ selected on eval set, not held-out)

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **introduction.tex** (lines 24-26):
     - C4 §1 novelty argument: community assumption + strongest test
     ```latex
     Prior work establishes that LLMs cannot self-correct without external feedback \citep{huang2024selfcorrect, stechly2025selfverification}, but concerns natural-language self-correction; neurosymbolic methods implicitly assume that formalizing into logic provides a reliable verification channel.
     We test the strongest version of this assumption: first-order logic checked by a provably sound SMT solver (Z3), which \emph{guarantees} logical consistency given well-formed constraints.
     That this stronger channel still fails is the central surprise: Z3 rejects only 3.4\% of constraints (\S\ref{sec:confirmation-bias}) because they are individually valid yet collectively biased---the bias is semantic (what gets extracted) rather than syntactic (how it is expressed).
     ```

   - **related_work.tex**:
     - C5 three paradigms + C4 SatLM control in neurosymbolic paragraph (line 8)
     - W7 ToT citation added to test-time compute paragraph (line 11): `\citep{snell2025scaling} or structured search \citep{yao2023tree}`
     - W6 SCB distinction in CJT paragraph (line 15): "Symbolic confirmation bias is distinct from CoT unfaithfulness \citep{turpin2024language} and CoT-level confirmation bias \citep{wan2025unveiling, jhaveri2026failing}"
     - miya2025eidoku added to recent extensions list

   - **solutions.tex**:
     - W1 DRC τ caveat (line 66 area): "Note that $\tau$ was selected on the evaluation set; deployment would require a held-out validation split."
     - W2 Cross-arch 3 conditions in "Why it works" paragraph: "(i) structural independence, (ii) positive capability gap, (iii) task-verifier alignment"

   - **experiments.tex**:
     - W4 TOST margin: "reflecting the smallest $\Delta$ we consider practically meaningful given SC baselines of 39--86%"
     - TOST correction: "4 equivalent, 2 genuinely different (both negative: Mistral-7B and Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter), 10 underpowered---reflecting the power limitations at $n{=}200$--$204$"
     - Table 1 footnote simplified

   - **analysis.tex**:
     - W8: 27 strategies "four categories---sampling diversity, extraction quality, aggregation, and multi-agent"
     - Figure 2 → figure* full-width
     - BR with CIs (line 47):
     ```latex
     Bias generalizes: $4.97\times$ [3.98, 6.37] (Mistral, 12-trace), $3.93\times$ [2.44, 7.11] (Qwen-14B, 12-trace), $2.88\times$ (LLaMA, 4-trace$^{\dag}$), all $> 1.0$ (95\% bootstrap CIs for Mistral/Qwen; Table~\ref{tab:cross-model-bias}; weighted BRs in Appendix~\ref{app:cross-model-bias}).
     ```

   - **method.tex** — CIL framework added after Observation 2 (after line 62):
     ```latex
     \paragraph{Cumulative Information Lift.}
     We introduce \textit{Cumulative Information Lift} (CIL) to unify these diagnostics under a single information-theoretic quantity:
     \begin{equation}
     \label{eq:cil}
     \text{CIL}(V, G) = \log \frac{P(V \text{ correct} \mid G \text{ wrong})}{P(V \text{ correct} \mid G \text{ correct})}.
     \end{equation}
     $\text{CIL} > 0$ means $V$ preferentially corrects $Gs errors; $\text{CIL} < 0$ indicates shared bias. CIL subsumes our findings: (1)~SCB corresponds to $\text{CIL}(\text{self}, G) \approx 0$; (2)~Observation~2 predicts $\text{CIL}(V, G) > 0$ when $V$ is independent and capable; (3)~DRC routes to $V$ where expected CIL is highest. Across [N] pairs, CIL correlates with combo gain ($\rho = $ [TBD], $p < $ [TBD]).
     ```

   - **discussion.tex** — Compressed from 4 paragraphs to 3 (merged "Implications for trained reasoning" into "Test-time scaling"):
     ```latex
     \paragraph{Self-verification generalization.}
     Our bias ratio ($4.97\times$ Mistral, $3.93\times$ Qwen, $2.88\times$ LLaMA) quantifies why self-correction fails without external feedback \citep{huang2024selfcorrect, stechly2025selfverification}: extraction and generation share distributional biases. $\text{BR} > 1$ across three families predicts that any self-verification pipeline deriving criteria from the same model faces this bottleneck, whether formal constraints, natural-language critiques, or code assertions.

     \paragraph{Test-time scaling.}
     $K_{\text{eff}} = 1.20$--$3.62$ for nominal $K = 12$ means sampling beyond a dozen traces yields diminishing independent information; the pattern intensifies with capability (Qwen3 thinking: $\kappa = 0.91$, $K_{\text{eff}} = 1.09$), creating a scaling paradox for o1/R1-style models \citep{guo2025deepseekr1}. All non-destructive interventions cluster at $\kappa \geq 0.40$, confirming a structural ceiling \citep{krogh1994neural}; Debate reaches $\kappa = 0.15$ but collapses accuracy ($-18.6$\,pp). Cross-architecture escape succeeds ($\rho = 1.0$, $p = 0.003$) because encoder-only and decoder-only models have structurally different error profiles. Trained reasoning internalization bypasses the bottleneck: Qwen3-14B thinking achieves 86\% on FOLIO, exceeding Mistral-7B's self-extraction ceiling (${\sim}62\%$; Bound~1).

     \paragraph{Practitioner implications.}
     Two diagnostics predict failure: $C_0 < 5\%$ means SICA reduces to SC; SC $\leq 40\%$ risks error amplification ($-2.83$\,pp). For intermediate-SC models, gain tracks the capability gap ($\rho = 1.0$, $p = 0.003$); the bottleneck is extraction quality, as oracle constraints succeed ($+29.90$\,pp, $+14.22$\,pp).
     ```

   - **limitations_content.tex** — W3 power note added:
     "McNemar power for detecting $|\Delta| = 2$\,pp is below 21\% at $n{=}200$--$600$; our tests are adequately powered only for $|\Delta| \geq 5$\,pp"

   - **appendix.tex**:
     - TOST section rewritten with new 4/2/10 classification + sensitivity table (±1pp/±2pp/±3pp)
     - LLaMA BR reverted to 2.88 in raw BR list
     - Added "LLaMA weighted BR CI: [2.19, 3.28]"
